newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt rises, cautiously awaits Thurs U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt rises, cautiously awaits Thurs U.S. data.

text.p: Emerging market debt rose modestly on Wednesday, but most investors remained sidelined before another round of U.S. economic reports, traders said.

Wednesday's much-awaited data on U.S. retail sales and wholesale inflation boosted emerging bonds early, they said. In the afternoon, however, the gains eased and spreads over comparable U.S. Treasuries generally widened.

"There were pretty heavy flows after the numbers, but since then it's quieted down," one Brady bond trader said. "The fact that the (U.S.) bond market and the currency market are so volatile is keeping people from doing a lot."
Certain long-dated Mexico Eurobonds saw buyers early in the session, traders said. "There's been good demand in the long end of Mexico," said one.
Mexico's UMS 2026 was quoted up one point at 120-1/2 in late trading. Mexico Brady bonds rose less strongly, with Pars up 5/8 at 80-3/8.

Russian debt tallied losses for the first time in several sessions. Dollar-denominated Vnesh loans slipped 1/4 to 101-7/8 as investors questioned how much up-side was left before the yearend London Club restructuring, traders said.
Ecuador Brady debt turned in a mixed performance. Pars were up 3/8 at 52-3/8 but IEBs slipped 1/4 to 91-1/2.

Through Tuesday, the Ecuador component of J.P. Morgan's Emerging Markets Bond Index (EMBI) fell 1.95 percent for August. Traders said they had not sighted concerted selling of the country's paper on Wednesday.
Elsewhere, Brazil "C" bonds were up 3/8 at 83-1/8 and Argentina FRBs were up 1/8 at 95-3/4.
Emerging debt and U.S. Treasuries jumped early Wednesday after reports showed U.S. producer prices declined for the seventh straight month in July, while retail sales came in near expectations.
Jitters about Thursday's data, however, foreshortened the market's rally, traders said.
On Thursday, investors will eye reports on the July U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI), as well as the Federal Reserve's assessment of July industrial production.

Economists surveyed by Reuters forecast CPI up 0.2 percent both overall and in its core components, which exclude volatile food and energy prices. They projected industrial production up 0.2 percent and capacity utilization at 83.5 percent.
